pr_title: Bluetooth: controller: fix failing EBQ scanner tests
pr_body:
In the case that chaining is enabled when adding new data to an advertising chain a new PDU is created for this data. This limits how often data can be added to the number of available PDUs.

The changes in this PR add the data to the last PDU in the chain, and only if there is not enough room a new PDU is created

A test was added to CI where the name is set to an extra long length to force an overflow of data to occur so that this new functionality is tested

See issues #63288 and #63290 for further improvements

fixes #59580
pr_comments:
@Tronil for some reason I can not reply to your comment regarding the calculation. Actually it is the right calculation, we substract ad_len_overflow_first_try from ad_len_overflow_first to find how much extra data is needed in the variable sized header.
But the code has become quite complicated and @cvinayak and I agree that this code needs a rewrite
@kruithofa Please also update the commit message for the first commit (and the PR title too) as "Bluetooth: controller: fix regression" is extremely generic :D

review_comments: OTOH val_ptr points to unsigned int. There are several other places in the code where 0U is used in memset. Let us discuss outside of this PR, and create another PR to fix all locations if that is what we agree on.
Doesn't really matter that much :) But it's just common to use `U` when doing unsigned, and omit it for signed values (like for `memset`).
What happens if we have a completely full PDU that we want to add an aux ptr to (ie. we now have to move some existing advertising data to the next PDU)? This code doesn't seem to handle that case.
That is handled by the ull_adv_aux_clear_set function. However this code is hard to follow, so we want to do a rewrite. See issue #63288 and #63290
Unless I am missing something, `ad_len_overflow_first_try` was removed, so this comment is no longer correct
